A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CodeSense and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. The shared material can be matched reliably, including the retained appendix analyses and v3's added Sections A.10–A.14.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 14 LLMs across six research questions, with additional prompting results and an API-definition ablation in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds cross-benchmark scores, repeated-run measurements, a prompting comparison, and a model-error example.

M1.justification: The tracing pipeline, ground-truth construction, semantic tasks, abstract-value mappings, and inference approach remain unchanged. The new experiments and expanded capability descriptions do not document a revised method component.

E1.justification: A.10/Table 9 adds evaluation on CruxEval's synthetic Python output-prediction task using three existing models. The original real-world Python, C, and Java coverage is retained.

E2.justification: A.12/Table 11 explicitly compares same-statement-type demonstrations against different-statement-type demonstrations, supplementing v2's random-versus-relevant comparison in RQ4. The fourteen-model roster and existing API-definition and random baselines remain unchanged; CoRe appears only in related-work positioning.

E3.justification: A.10 introduces a partial cross-benchmark evaluation restricted to three existing models, and A.12 specifies a different-statement-type demonstration control. Existing sample counts, accuracy scoring, and inference parameters are retained. A.13 newly documents function-size thresholds without establishing that the original size-based evaluation changed.

E4.justification: A.12 adds evidence about sensitivity to demonstration statement type. A.14 adds a concrete failure case: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B predicts 10 loop iterations for an eleven-character string. The earlier prompting analyses and API-definition ablation remain present.

E5.justification: A.11/Table 10 newly reports three statement-prediction runs and means with standard deviations for four models. v2 provides no corresponding run-count or uncertainty reporting; this does not establish how many runs underlay v2. The new reporting is limited to one task and a model subset.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces several Python scores: Gr-3.2 variable-assignment accuracy changes from approximately 0.59 to 0.15, without an explained setting change. Tables 9–11 add cross-benchmark, repeated-run, and prompting results, while A.14 adds an observed error. For example, Table 9 reports DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B at 0.75 on CruxEval and 0.37 on CodeSense; these are different-dataset results, not a version-to-version performance decline.

T1.justification: The semantic definitions and concrete-to-abstract mappings are retained. Neither version presents theoretical proofs or guarantees, and the new empirical size categories and code example do not introduce a theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and headline conclusions retain the same benchmark and model-weakness claims. However, the expanded introductory Table 1 newly asserts multi-file-context support for CodeSense, adding an explicit capability claim without a corresponding documented method change.

C2.justification: v3 removes Section 2.2's assertion that generated dynamic values have never been seen by the models. A.11 newly interprets the findings as stable across runs, and A.14 attributes an iteration-prediction failure to character miscounting. The substantive limitations in A.2 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: A.13/Table 12 newly supplies thresholds for the existing small, medium, and large function categories: at most 9 lines, more than 10 through 19 lines, and at least 20 lines. This disclosure leaves length 10 unassigned. Hardware, inference configurations, tracing instructions, prompt templates, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Table 1 adds CoRe, expands the benchmark feature comparison, and changes CodeMind's real-world-projects characterization from unsupported to supported. The Valgrind discussion and its two Nethercote references are removed. The broader related-work narrative remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 replaces part of the introduction's motivation with a benchmark-construction summary, removes the leakage paragraph, makes localized language and citation edits, and appends A.10–A.14. Most existing sections and appendix explanations retain their wording and organization.

P2.justification: Table 1 is expanded and relocated, Figure 4's Python panel is redrawn with revised styling and an expanded displayed model selection, and Tables 9–12 are added. Several main-text figures move closer to their discussions. The remaining figure assets and original appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The CruxEval comparison, limited three-run analysis, and concrete failure example provide useful additional support, while the redrawn Figure 4 improves readability. These are modest gains, limited by new reporting inconsistencies: the introduction states 4,495 samples while Table 2 retains 4,483, and Table 10 gives a 38.3% mean for three 38.4% runs. Some settings for the added comparisons also remain unspecified.
